title: How VRR Makes a Monitor Wait for the GPU
description:
Variable refresh rate does not make the GPU faster. It lets a compatible display begin a refresh when a frame is ready. This short animation explains the VRR operating window, why low and high frame rates still matter and which parts of the display path must support it.

Sources:
https://vesa.org/featured-articles/vesa-adds-adaptive-sync-to-popular-displayport-video-standard/
https://gpuopen.com/manuals/fidelityfx_sdk/techniques/frame-interpolation-swap-chain/
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddxgi/variable-refresh-rate-displays

Visuals: original Pulse Gaming diagrams.
